audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph Judah and Caleb/Jerahmeel genealogies, first-pass restored draft with public-domain scaffold; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Judah's sons, Tamar, David's siblings, women and concubines, Jarha the Egyptian servant, daughter inheritance through marriage, towns and territorial language, artisan and scribal families, and textual variants.

verses.restored: These are sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
Sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; these three were born to him from daughter of Shua the Canaanite. Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in eyes of YHWH, and YHWH put him to death.
Tamar his daughter-in-law bore him Perez and Zerah. All sons of Judah were five.
Sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul.
Sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara—five in all.
Son of Carmi: Achar/Achan, troubler of Israel, who acted unfaithfully concerning devoted thing.
Son of Ethan: Azariah.
Sons born to Hezron: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai/Caleb.
Ram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, leader of children of Judah.
Nahshon fathered Salma, and Salma fathered Boaz.
Boaz fathered Obed, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse fathered Eliab his firstborn, Abinadab second, Shimea third,
Nethanel fourth, Raddai fifth,
Ozem sixth, David seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. Sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three.
Abigail bore Amasa; father of Amasa was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron fathered children through Azubah his wife and Jerioth; her sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
Azubah died, and Caleb took Ephrath, who bore Hur to him.
Hur fathered Uri, and Uri fathered Bezalel.
Afterward Hezron went to daughter of Machir father of Gilead; he took her when sixty years old, and she bore Segub to him.
Segub fathered Jair, who had twenty-three cities in land of Gilead.
Geshur and Aram took Havvoth-jair from them, with Kenath and its villages—sixty cities. All these belonged to descendants of Machir father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb-ephrathah, Abijah wife of Hezron bore Ashhur father of Tekoa.
Sons of Jerahmeel firstborn of Hezron were Ram firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah; she was mother of Onam.
Sons of Ram firstborn of Jerahmeel were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
Sons of Onam were Shammai and Jada. Sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur.
Name of Abishur's wife was Abihail; she bore Ahban and Molid to him.
Sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; Seled died without children.
Son of Appaim: Ishi. Son of Ishi: Sheshan. Child/descendant of Sheshan: Ahlai.
Sons of Jada brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; Jether died without children.
Sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These were descendants of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, but daughters. Sheshan had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter to Jarha his servant as wife, and she bore Attai to him.
Attai fathered Nathan, and Nathan fathered Zabad,
Zabad fathered Ephlal, and Ephlal fathered Obed,
Obed fathered Jehu, and Jehu fathered Azariah,
Azariah fathered Helez, and Helez fathered Eleasah,
Eleasah fathered Sismai, and Sismai fathered Shallum,
Shallum fathered Jekamiah, and Jekamiah fathered Elishama.
Sons of Caleb brother of Jerahmeel: Mesha his firstborn, father of Ziph; and sons of Mareshah father of Hebron.
Sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema fathered Raham father of Jorkeam; Rekem fathered Shammai.
Son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was father of Beth-zur.
Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; Haran fathered Gazez.
Sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph father of Madmannah, Sheva father of Machbenah and Gibea; daughter of Caleb was Achsah.
These were descendants of Caleb. Sons of Hur firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal father of Kiriath-jearim,
Salma father of Bethlehem, and Hareph father of Beth-gader.
Shobal father of Kiriath-jearim had descendants: Haroeh and half of Menuhoth.
Families of Kiriath-jearim were Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites; from them came Zorathites and Eshtaolites.
Descendants of Salma: Bethlehem, Netophathites, Atroth-beth-joab, half of Manahathites, and Zorites.
Families of scribes who lived at Jabez: Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Sucathites. These were Kenites who came from Hammath, father of house of Rechab.

translation_notes: The genealogy repeatedly includes women, sisters, wives, concubines, daughters, migrants, artisans, and scribes even though its grammar is largely patrilineal.
Tamar's appearance must be read with Genesis 38; she is not a sexual scandal inserted into David's line but a survivor who secured justice and descendants within a coercive patriarchal system.
Er's death and Achar/Achan's label are narrator theology and must not justify summary punishment or lifelong family stigma.
Jarha is explicitly an Egyptian servant. His enslavement or servile status must not be romanticized; his incorporation into the genealogy does not erase coercive power around his marriage.
Sheshan's daughter is unnamed while her husband and descendants are named. The archive's omission should be acknowledged rather than treating women as mere transmission points.
Territorial statements about Gilead, Geshur, Aram, and towns preserve contested political memory, not timeless property deeds.
Concubine language signals unequal household status and requires care around consent and reproductive power.
Names and kinship structures vary across Hebrew manuscripts, Greek witnesses, Samuel/Kings parallels, and modern reconstructions.
safety_note: Do not use this chapter to defend patriarchy, slavery, coerced marriage, concubinage, inherited shame, blood purity, or modern territorial claims. Center Tamar, unnamed daughters, Jarha, women whose bodies carry the genealogy, and communities displaced or absorbed by elite households.
